title: Epic Sepsis Model external validation at a large health system
system_purpose: Predict sepsis onset in hospitalized patients and alert clinicians
decision_impact: Alerts shape whether clinicians investigate and escalate a deteriorating patient
verified_facts: An external validation across 27697 patients and 38455 hospitalizations found the proprietary sepsis model performed far below the vendor-reported range, with poor discrimination and heavy alert burden.
reported_harm: Late or missed recognition of deterioration plus alert fatigue that erodes trust in the tool
quantitative_evidence: AUC 0.63 with 95 percent CI 0.62 to 0.64; sensitivity 33 percent; positive predictive value 12 percent; alerts on 6971 of 38455 hospitalizations or 18 percent; 1709 of 2552 sepsis patients or 67 percent not identified.
limitations: One academic health system and a retrospective design; the study measures model performance, not clinician response, and a later model version may behave differently.

title: Speech-to-text hallucinations in transcription of impaired speech
system_purpose: Transcribe recorded speech into text for downstream use including patient notes
decision_impact: Transcript errors propagate into records that later readers treat as what was actually said
affected_groups: patients with speech impairments;clinicians reading notes
verified_facts: A peer-reviewed audit of a leading speech-to-text service found whole fabricated sentences that were absent from the source audio, concentrated among speakers with longer non-vocal durations.
reported_harm: Fabricated content entering a record and false attribution of statements to a speaker
quantitative_evidence: Roughly 1 percent of transcriptions contained entire hallucinated phrases; 38 percent of hallucinations included explicit harms such as invented violence or false authority.
limitations: The audit used an aphasia speech corpus and a general service as of 2023 rather than a deployed hospital scribe, so clinical harm is foreseeable rather than documented.

title: Eating disorder helpline chatbot suspended after harmful advice
system_purpose: Provide automated wellbeing guidance to people contacting a helpline
decision_impact: Automated guidance reached vulnerable help seekers with no clinician in the loop
affected_groups: people seeking eating disorder help;helpline staff and volunteers
verified_facts: Two independent outlets report that the Tessa chatbot was taken offline days after launch and that NEDA's own CEO stated the deployed version may have given information that was harmful; its designer said it was scripted and not as sophisticated as a large generative model.
reported_harm: Reported harm: weight-loss and body-fat guidance served to people seeking eating-disorder help, which can worsen a diagnosed condition for a vulnerable group with no clinician reviewing the response
quantitative_evidence: One outlet quotes specific advice of 1 to 2 pounds of weekly weight loss and caliper body-fat measurement; both outlets agree the bot replaced 6 paid staff and about 200 volunteers on a helpline that served nearly 70000 people the prior year, though neither states which calendar year that prior-year figure covers.
limitations: Both sources are press reporting quoting the same NEDA statement rather than an independent technical audit of chatbot outputs or a regulator finding, the designer described the system as rule-based and scripted rather than a large language model, and no source gives a denominator for how many help seekers received harmful versus safe responses.
